survey: A pocket calculator floating against a pi-pattern background. The body is a thick, rounded slab rotated about 15° clockwise in the picture plane. The camera sits almost square to its front face, with a slight offset that shows a sliver of thickness along the left and bottom edges. The top and bottom edges of the face are about the same length, so the face is not noticeably tilted away from the viewer. Three parts sit on the face: a red solar strip and a grey display window near the top, both aligned with the body's rotated top edge, and below them a 4×4 keypad. The keypad has three columns of blue keys and one column of cyan keys on the right. Each key row runs parallel to the body's top and bottom edges, and each column runs parallel to its side edges. Because the face is nearly square to the camera, keys of equal size are correct. Every key shows its thickness on the same lower-left side as the body does, so the keys, the display, the solar strip and the slab all agree on one viewpoint. There is no ground plane, so contact does not apply.
